steps.title: Soft and plummy
steps.body: Merlot gives medium to full-bodied reds with plum, black cherry, blackberry and, with oak, chocolate and vanilla. Tannins are softer than Cabernet Sauvignon's, acidity medium. It's approachable young and can age well when grown on great sites. It's the second most planted red grape in the world.

steps.title: Origins
steps.body: Merlot comes from Bordeaux, first recorded in 1784. Its name may come from merle, the French for blackbird, which loves its ripe grapes. DNA shows its parents are Cabernet Franc and Magdeleine Noire des Charentes, so it's a half-sibling of Cabernet Sauvignon. Its large, thinner-skinned berries explain its softer tannins.

steps.prompt: Where may Merlot's name come from?
steps.explanation: Merle means blackbird, a bird that loves its ripe grapes.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for medium to deep ruby colour, plum and black cherry aromas, and a rounder, softer palate than Cabernet, with less obvious blackcurrant. Cool-climate Merlot can show herbal or green notes; warm-climate Merlot is ripe and fruity, sometimes jammy.

steps.prompt: Merlot has larger berries and thinner skins than Cabernet Sauvignon.
steps.explanation: Yes. That's why its tannins are softer and its wines rounder.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Merlot gives plum, black cherry and soft tannins
It comes from Bordeaux; its name may mean blackbird
It's a half-sibling of Cabernet Sauvignon
